Observations below are retained unedited as recorded on 2026-08-01 and are no longer a live evidence requirement.

scopesOrPermissions: business_management when the selected business-management endpoint requires it
sourceObservations.finding: The setup flow depends on business assets and granted app permissions; no repository artifact proves ownership, review, or a production-capable token.

scopesOrPermissions: webhook subscription for only the WhatsApp fields consumed by the adapter

observed app permission grant and least-privilege token

metaWhatsApp.fallback: Use authenticated Atelier workflows and manual customer communication; no automated WhatsApp delivery.

prerequisites: bot token issued by BotFather, stored outside Git
public HTTPS callback that can receive a real update
scopesOrPermissions: allowed_updates limited to the update types the product actually consumes
sourceObservations.finding: Authentication is a single bot token; there is no business portfolio, owned phone-number asset, app review, permission grant, template approval, or customer-service window. setWebhook accepts a secret_token of 1-256 characters from A-Za-z0-9_- that Telegram returns in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header on every webhook request, and update_id is documented as the basis for ignoring repeated updates and restoring order.

scopesOrPermissions: adapter reads and sends only through the single bot identity it is configured with
sourceObservations.finding: The official Telegram adapter documents the bot token as its only required credential and validates incoming webhook requests against the secret token configured through setWebhook. Documented platform constraints are callback data limited to 64 bytes and fetchMessages returning only adapter-cached messages from the current process.

prerequisites: pinned adapter and SDK versions with a reviewed dependency and build-script policy
scopesOrPermissions: no provider entitlement is conferred by the package itself
sourceObservations.finding: Version 4.36.0 is published from the vercel/chat repository directory packages/adapter-telegram, depending exactly on chat@4.36.0 and @chat-adapter/shared@4.36.0 with engines.node >=20, published 2026-08-01. Package availability proves a pinnable candidate exists and proves nothing about provider delivery or authenticity.

scopesOrPermissions: getMe and getWebhookInfo called against the live bot identity; no webhook registered
sourceObservations.finding: Live getMe returned ok:true for is_bot:true username Sammysfavorites_bot first_name Daisy4sammy with bot id retained only as sha256:f3ba8c6512ad33f7f7fde99d2a1d8f4ada68e75f99f6b923e0b68f3dfd9f0caf. getWebhookInfo shows webhook_configured:false and pending_update_count:0. credentialMaterialPresent is false in the repository. This is provider_observed identity and webhook-absent evidence; it does not clear G0. Remaining receipts: public HTTPS setWebhook, real inbound update, negative secret header, duplicate update_id, outbound sendMessage.

requiredEvidence: getMe receipt establishing bot identity, hashed, retaining only non-secret fields
registered webhook with secret_token and minimal allowed_updates, evidenced by getWebhookInfo
real inbound update with a constant-time X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token comparison outcome
negative case: an update with a wrong or absent secret header is rejected
repeated update_id idempotently ignored, with business-effect count and reconciliation result
outbound sendMessage delivery receipt
receipt minted for provider telegram through the existing WebhookVerificationRepository
telegram.securityNote: The Telegram header secret is a bearer credential, not an HMAC over the payload. It proves the caller knows the secret but does not bind to the body and leaves no re-verifiable per-message artifact. Compensating controls are recorded in ADR 0003.
telegram.fallback: Automated messaging stays disabled; the authenticated Atelier surface and manual customer communication remain the operating position.
